title: Snap a specimen swab's handle off at its breakpoint in a free-standing transport tube, and bin the handle
instruction: Snap the swab's handle off at its breakpoint, leaving the swab's tip in the transport tube, and drop the handle in the waste cup. Leave the tube standing.
context: Breaking the swab off in its tube ends every throat, nose or wound swab collection. Collecting and preparing specimens is a core task of medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00, over 800,000 US workers) and routine for registered nurses and phlebotomists. The maker's directions: hold the tube, hold the end of the shaft, bend it to break at the breakpoint. The instruction leaves the holding unsaid. The open tube with its medium weighs 10 g on a 16 mm base: a 0.007 N push on the handle tips it, while snapping the shaft takes about 1.1 N. The shaft must also snap with the tip down in the tube, where the breakpoint sits just inside the rim; lifted first, it snaps with the specimen in the air. The handle is 2.5 mm thick and only leans on the rim, so a touch moves it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Transport tube: 16 x 100 mm skirted, free-standing, cap off, clear plastic with a white skirt, wall 1.25 mm (bore 13.5 mm), inside floor 12 mm above the table; it holds 3 mL of orange-pink transport medium (21 mm deep); tube and medium 10 g; base centred at x 26, y -10 (layout A) or x 28, y -8 (layout B, environment variable SWAB_LOT=B). Swab: a regular flocked swab 15 cm long, about 1.1 g: white flocked tip 5.5 mm across and 16 mm long on a white plastic shaft 2.5 mm across, with a moulded breakpoint 80 mm from the tip marked by a red ring. It stands in the tube, tip in the middle of the tube's floor, shaft leaning on the far side of the rim (3.4 degrees from upright, away from the robot); the breakpoint is 8 mm below the rim and the handle sticks 6 cm out. Waste cup: open grey plastic cup, 10 cm across inside, 8 cm tall, 20 g, base centred at x 32, y -30. Nothing is fixed to the table. Both arms start in the raised ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Tools: side video with a ruler in view, a protractor, a ruler. 0 if the handle has not come off the rest of the swab; or if, in the last frame before it came off, the swab's tip was outside the tube or more than 15 mm above the tube's inside floor (the red ring at the breakpoint more than 7 mm above the rim; it sits 8 mm below the rim when the tip is on the floor) or the tube was more than 45 degrees from upright; or if at any time the tube was more than 60 degrees from upright (spilled) or the swab's tip was outside the tube. Otherwise 0.5: the handle is off. 0.75: and at the end the handle's middle is inside the waste cup (below its rim, within its inside diameter) with the cup within 30 degrees of upright. 1.0: and the tube stands on the table within 5 degrees of upright, its base no more than 3 mm off the table, with the tip inside it; the tube, both lengths of the swab and the cup are at rest (under 2 cm/s); and no part of either gripper is within 3 cm of the tube or of the handle.
reset_notes: Each trial uses up one swab. Seat a new swab with its tip on the tube's floor and its handle leaning away from the robot, stand the open tube on its mark and empty the waste cup. Top the medium up to 3 mL if any was lost.
fidelity: Tube, the swab's two lengths and cup are loose rigid bodies. The breakpoint is a joint that lets go for good at 0.03 N m of bending or 60 N of pull, calculated for a 1.5 mm polystyrene neck, not measured; a real shaft bends further before it snaps. Tube size, 3 mL and the 80 mm breakpoint are catalogue figures; shaft, tip, wall and masses are estimates. The medium is drawn, not simulated: its weight is in the tube, and tilt past 60 degrees counts as a spill. Capping is left out.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers reached toward the tube and the waste cup, then drew back; the swab was left whole in the standing tube); demo: 1.0 (layout A, full score at step 532; layout B also reaches 1.0, at step 442)
